subject: Orbitary integration: probe plan and solution assertions
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@orbitary.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Orbitary integration: probe plan and solution assertions

Alex —

Thanks for agreeing to run a short technical probe with us. Attached is a lightweight checklist that covers the reference-design acceptance criteria we'd like to validate up front (auth, data plane isolation, performance smoke, and graceful fallback). High level ask: confirm we can run a 2-hour interop window where Redwood will exercise your adapter against a staging environment and validate routing, KV/prefix cache behavior, and throughput under a 50-user simulated burst.

Quick proposed scope and timeline:
- Tuesday 2026-05-19: 2-hour interop window (10:00–12:00 PT)
- Tests: connectivity + auth, streaming/generator pass, prefix cache re-use, brief quantized run for memory check
- Success criteria: model responses within 350ms p50 (when routed to the low-latency path), no data leakage to external systems, and no more than 5% error rate on 500 requests

To make the window productive we need:
- a staging endpoint or connector image we can hit (whitelist our Redwood test IPs)
- a test corpus (100 short prompts + 20 chat sessions)
- a SRE contact for incident routing (for real-time log access)

I'm attaching the interop checklist and a proposed micro runbook. Can you confirm the window and share the SRE contact? If the 19th doesn't work we'll move to the 20th.

Attachment: interop-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
Attachment: redwood-orbitary-ma-plan.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
From: Alex Novak <alex.novak@orbitary.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orbitary Engineering <eng-team@orbitary.io>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@orbitary.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-17T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orbitary integration: probe plan and solution assertions

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the plan and the checklist. We can do the 2-hour window on 2026-05-19 10:00–12:00 PT. We've looped in Priya (SRE) and the eng-team for the session. Quick notes/questions from our side:

- We will expose a staging connector endpoint (https://staging.orbitary.io/redwood-probe) and can whitelist Redwood IPs.
- For telemetry, can you confirm the specific log artifacts you'll need? We can stream request/response traces and per-request latency. Our typical fields: request_id, route, model_version, start_ts, latency_ms, error_code.
- Model compatibility: we're currently running a trimmed Llama-3 variant and a 7B quantized variant. Which model(s) does Redwood need us to exercise?
- We need the list of prompts to run through — can you upload to the Drive folder or share a signed link?

We'll share the connector image tag and a service account for temporary access (token TTL 24h). Priya: can you coordinate SRE side for real-time Slack channel?

Attachment: none (we will upload the connector smoke image to the shared Drive)

—Alex
Alex Novak
Head of Integrations, Orbitary Inc
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@orbitary.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orbitary integration: probe plan and solution assertions

Alex — thanks, that timeline works. A few details to make the session deterministic:

- Redwood will exercise two model flows: generation (Llama-3-trim) and a quantized inference path (7B-quant). If the 7B path has memory constraints we'll fall back to a shorter context test.
- Telemetry: the fields you listed are perfect. We'll want per-request start_ts, end_ts, route, model_version, and any KV-cache hits flagged (boolean). Please stream traces to the shared Drive bucket or enable log access to our SRE account.
- Credentials: a service account token with 24h TTL works. We'll prefer a short-lived token via your Vault; if that's not available, a pre-signed key is ok for the window.
- Success criteria (restating): p50 latency < 350ms on the low-latency path, p95 < 800ms for burst; KV cache reuse >= 45% across the prompt set; no authentication failures; no unexpected outbound egress logs.

I've uploaded the test corpus (100 prompts + 20 chat threads) to the Drive link below. We'll also attach the interop-runbook to the session invite.

Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_EXAMPLE_ORBITARY
Attachment: interop-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Karthik
Principal Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@orbitary.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orbitary integration: probe plan and solution assertions

Alex/Karthik —

A couple of operational notes from the partner success side before the probe:

- Canary policy: if the 2-hour window is green, we propose a staged canary (5% traffic for 24h -> 25% for 48h -> full routing) for the first production cutover. We'll draft the rollback playbook and share.
- Cost/Quota: Orbitary's adapter will be routed to a low-latency pool; Sergio, please confirm estimated token throughput so we can model committed capacity for Dedicated if/when they go live.
- Contracts: we'll need a short addendum for telemetry-sharing and retention. Legal will send a 1-page attachment; Alex, we'll include that in the DocuSign packet.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.

—Marissa
Director, Partner Success, Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orbitary integration: probe plan and solution assertions

Internal —

Following up on capacity estimates: based on the proposed 50-user simulated burst and the 500-request smoke load, we should be fine on shared hosted for the probe. If Orbitary expects sustained production traffic at >2k rps we'll need to provision a Dedicated pool (estimate: 2x A100-equivalents for steady-state, ramp to 3x for peak). I'm going to coordinate with Infra to reserve a small Dedicated slot for a potential canary (DEV-Dedicated:EDGE-2).

I'll draft a short capacity note and attach to the canary playbook.

—Sergio
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Novak <alex.novak@orbitary.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orbitary integration: probe plan and solution assertions

Thanks everyone — confirming the 2026-05-19 session went well and we're green on the core flows. A few closing points from Orbitary:

- We've uploaded the signed limited-access SRE token for the 2-hour window and a zipped capture-log from our side: capture-log-20260518.txt (plain text).
- We shared the test corpus at the Drive link and granted your service account read access.
- Two caveats before production routing: 1) we need a short PII redaction step on the Redwood side for any free-text user fields (we propose a regex-based filter at the gateway), and 2) the 7B-quant run produced occasional out-of-memory logs at high context lengths — we recommend limiting context to 1024 tokens for the quantized path until we ship a memory-optimized adapter.

DocuSign: envelope-0d9f-23a has been sent — it's the access & telemetry addendum. Once signed, we'll schedule the canary cutover as proposed by Marissa.

Attachment: capture-log-20260518.txt (text/plain)

—Alex
Head of Integrations, Orbitary Inc
